## Linux measurement in the MCP image (option chosen 2026-10-28: measure before sizing a fix)

Image built from `infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp` at `f8ddcaf88e6` (Python 3.12, glibc), run locally on arm64 against an isolated clone of the tickets store, one fresh container per scenario. Peak = `VmHWM`, after = `VmRSS` after `gc.collect()`. Wall-clock times are omitted: the host was heavily loaded by an unrelated workload, so they do not carry over.

| 9 `next_batch` calls | Peak | After |
|---|---|---|
| sequential | 583 MB | 513 MB |
| at most 3 at once | 1,689 MB | 307 MB |
| at most 4 at once | 2,234 MB | 320 MB |
| at most 5 at once | 2,776 MB | 676 MB |
| at most 6 at once | 3,323 MB | 477 MB |
| all 9 at once | 4,966 MB | 201 MB |
| all 9, second burst in the same process | 4,967 MB | 620 MB |
| all 9, then `malloc_trim(0)` | 4,965 MB | 182 MB |

- Each additional concurrent call adds about 545 MB at peak on this 5,759-ticket store.
- On Linux the memory returns after the calls; a second burst peaks no higher than the first, and `malloc_trim` changes little. The 3 GB retention seen on macOS does not carry over.
- So the box's 2-hour 3.2 GB plateau is not these reads. On the box, memory rose 0.93 to 3.28 GB between 15:29 and 15:34 PDT while only pings arrived. Filed as unmedical-stational-chrysalis.
